display.title: The Negel Vasser Test, Part 3 (Parshas Terumah)
display.summary_short: Making your room a Mikdash Me'at, as the Rebbe asked; then Matzliach frees two captives from the robbers' cave and sees how negel vasser saved his life twice.
display.summary_long: After the song "I Believe in Hashem", the storyteller turns to Parshas Terumah: Hashem said He would dwell "in them", in every Jew. In 5747 the Rebbe made an urgent personal request that every child make his room a Mikdash Me'at, with his own Chumash, siddur and pushka, and a Tanya too, marked with his name, using the room for Torah, tefillah and tzedakah. The Shulchan Aruch gives another reason for negel vasser: each morning we are like a Kohen washing before the service in the Beis HaMikdash. The story concludes. In the robbers' cave Matzliach finds the caravan captain and a young prince tied to the wall. The captain fears revenge, but Matzliach uses a sword only to cut their ropes. The prince tells how the robbers killed his soldiers and demanded a ransom from his father, the sheikh. Matzliach devises a plan to capture the gang when it returns. The grateful sheikh offers him his daughter and half his kingdom, but Matzliach, a Jew with a family, wants only to go home, and returns laden with gifts. He tells his children that negel vasser saved his life twice, and that the main reward of a mitzvah is in Olam Haba.
display.lesson: Make your own room a Mikdash Me'at with a Chumash, siddur and pushka. Negel vasser prepares us to serve Hashem, and a mitzvah protects the one who keeps it.
